messages.content: Complete the following case-report text from the exact point where it stops. Return only the most likely original continuation, without repeating the supplied text, adding headings, quoting the prompt, or explaining your approach. This is a text-continuation task. Write up to 234 whitespace-separated words.

Curative-intent ifosfamide, cisplatin, and etoposide (ICE) was started because of the prolonged remission, biopsy-proven recurrence, and anticipated chemosensitivity. The planned 28-day regimen comprised ifosfamide 900 mg/m2, cisplatin 20 mg/m2, and etoposide 100 mg/m2 on days 1–5. Scheduled oral desmopressin 360 μg/day, hydrocortisone 30 mg/day, and levothyroxine 50 μg/day were continued during the sodium disturbances following endocrinology consultation, which supported maintenance of the established doses and schedules. Before salvage chemotherapy, serum sodium was 139.3 mEq/L, measured serum osmolality was 278 mOsm/kg, serum creatinine was 0.52 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate was 163.4 mL/min/1.73 m2, spot urinary sodium was 91.4 mEq/L, and urine osmolality was 555 mOsm/kg. Baseline cortisol was reported as 5.5 μg/dL, but sampling time relative to hydrocortisone was unavailable, and the value was not used to infer adrenal reserve. Baseline laboratory results are provided in Online Resource 3. The course of serum sodium and serum osmolality, oral sodium supplementation, treatment modifications, and urinary sodium/osmolality trends during ICE are shown in Fig. 3a, b. After ICE cycle 1, fatigue, anorexia, and headache accompanied grade 4 hypotonic hyponatremia (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events [CTCAE] version 5.0): serum sodium reached 118.4 mEq/L on cycle 1 day 9, and measured serum osmolality was 236 mOsm/kg. message.content: Output volumes were 2.5–3.5 L/day, with spot urinary sodium of 84.2 mEq/L and urine osmolality of 512 mOsm/kg, consistent with an ongoing sodium-wasting pattern rather than dilutional hyponatremia. Hypertonic saline was not required; instead, oral sodium chloride tablets were initiated and up-titrated, fluid intake was liberalized rather than restricted, and desmopressin was continued at the established dose, given the presumed combined central diabetes insipidus and cerebral salt-wasting physiology. Serum sodium corrected gradually to 132 mEq/L by cycle 1 day 14 and normalized before cycle 2. Hydrocortisone was empirically increased to 50 mg/day during the nadir, then returned to 30 mg/day after clinical improvement, without evidence of adrenal crisis. ICE cycle 2 proceeded at full doses on schedule. During cycle 2, serum sodium declined again to a nadir of 124.6 mEq/L on day 8, with similar urinary sodium and osmolality findings, and again responded to intensified oral sodium supplementation without hypertonic saline or desmopressin adjustment. Cycles 3 and 4 were complicated by milder hyponatremia (nadir 130–133 mEq/L), managed with continued oral sodium chloride and stable endocrine replacement. The patient completed all four planned ICE cycles without dose reduction or treatment delay attributable to sodium disturbances. Restaging imaging after completion of salvage chemotherapy showed no evidence of recurrent disease, and the patient remained in remission at follow-up. Throughout treatment, the collaborative endocrine management strategy—maintaining scheduled desmopressin, hydrocortisone, and levothyroxine while titrating oral sodium supplementation—prevented severe neurologic complications and allowed delivery of curative-intent chemotherapy without compromise.
